data.narrative:
CesiumAstro, a Series C-stage space and aerospace company that has raised $470M to date, was valued using two applicable triangulation methods against a comparable universe of 6 private peers in the same sector and stage proximity, supplemented by 5 public Space & Aerospace trading comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL).

Stage-progression analysis applied a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $470M total raised proxy, yielding $799M. Peer-median valuation across 6 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private comparables produced $1.8B, with a range spanning $1.15B to $8.0B; the wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity in business models and maturity within frontier aerospace. Public-comparable anchoring proved inapplicable due to absence of disclosed revenue for the target. Public sector peers trade at a 25.3x median price-to-sales multiple, which cannot be applied without revenue disclosure.

The two applicable methods triangulate to a median valuation of $1.3B, with a 25th–75th percentile range of $679M to $2.1B. Key uncertainties include CesiumAstro's revenue run-rate relative to peer benchmarks, the sustainability of the high valuation multiples observed in Sierra Space ($8.0B) and adjacent-stage comparables, and stage-specific capital efficiency. The $1.3B median represents a 1.75x step from raised capital, consistent with Series C progression norms but dependent on execution and market conditions in frontier aerospace.
